01-intro-to-pm.q: A project is best defined as…
options: An ongoing, repetitive activity that sustains an organization
A temporary endeavor to produce a unique product, service, or result
Any work assigned to a team
01-intro-to-pm.explain: Temporary = defined start and end. Unique = not routine, repeated output.

01-intro-to-pm.q: Which of these is an example of operations rather than a project?
options: Relocating IT infrastructure to the cloud
01-intro-to-pm.explain: Operations are ongoing and repetitive: order processing, accounts receivable/payable, equipment maintenance.

01-intro-to-pm.q: What is the relationship between a project and a product?
options: The project is how you get there; the product is the quantifiable result you end up with
The product is temporary; the project is permanent
The application of knowledge, skills, tools and techniques to project activities to meet project requirements

01-intro-to-pm.q: Which three approaches does PMI say teams use to deliver outcomes?
Project management balances desired results against constraints. Which are the constraints in this framing?
01-intro-to-pm.explain: Desired results = scope, performance, quality. Constraints = time, cost.

01-intro-to-pm.q: Which is NOT one of the five competing factors every project must deliver on?
01-intro-to-pm.explain: The five: scope, time, cost, quality, expectations (stakeholder approval).

01-intro-to-pm.q: In the five competing factors, "Expectations" refers to…
Compressing a project's schedule is most likely to…
options: Have no effect on other factors
Put pressure on cost or quality
01-intro-to-pm.explain: The factors pull against each other — pulling on one affects the others.

02-the-project-manager.q: How many project management processes does PMI define?
Process groups describe the ____, while knowledge areas describe the ____.
What is the correct order of the five process groups?
options: Planning → Initiating → Executing → Closing → Monitoring & Controlling
Initiating → Planning → Executing → Monitoring & Controlling → Closing
Initiating → Executing → Planning → Closing → Monitoring & Controlling
Planning → Executing → Initiating → Monitoring & Controlling → Closing

02-the-project-manager.q: Which process group hands off deliverables and archives lessons learned?
Which is NOT one of the ten knowledge areas?
02-the-project-manager.explain: The ten: Integration, Scope, Schedule, Cost, Quality, Resource, Communications, Risk, Procurement, Stakeholder.

02-the-project-manager.q: Which knowledge area "does the most work" and stitches the other nine together?
02-the-project-manager.explain: Develop Project Charter, Develop PM Plan, Direct & Manage Work, Integrated Change Control and Close Project are all Integration.

02-the-project-manager.q: The project management mindset's six principles fall into which three groups?
"Embed quality into processes and deliverables" belongs to which mindset group?
02-the-project-manager.explain: Proactive: holistic view + embed quality. Ownership: accountable leader + empowered culture. Value-Driven: focus on value + sustainability.

02-the-project-manager.q: In the sustainability pyramid, what is the preferred first option for a negative outcome?
What are the three legs of the PMI Talent Triangle?
options: Ways of Working, Business Acumen, Power Skills

02-the-project-manager.q: Performing ROI and NPV cost-benefit analyses falls under which Talent Triangle leg?
Selecting and tailoring a predictive, adaptive or hybrid delivery approach is part of…
According to the notes, communication can take up to what share of a project manager's job?

03-project-initiation-part-1.q: Which two processes make up the Initiating process group?
options: Develop Project Charter and Identify Stakeholders
Develop Project Management Plan and Collect Requirements
Identify Risks and Plan Risk Responses
Only someone who invests money in the project
An individual, group or organization that may affect, be affected, or perceive itself to be affected by the project
Only members of the development team

03-project-initiation-part-1.q: Where are the findings of Identify Stakeholders recorded?
When can you stop identifying stakeholders?
options: Only after the project is closed
03-project-initiation-part-1.explain: New stakeholders can surface even at deployment or when the product moves to operations.

03-project-initiation-part-1.q: Which stakeholder grid is the most common?
A stakeholder with high power can…
options: Cancel the project or change its direction

03-project-initiation-part-1.q: In a power/interest grid, "interest" refers to…
options: How much the stakeholder likes the project
The level and frequency of information the stakeholder needs about the project

03-project-initiation-part-1.q: The salience model classifies stakeholders on which three variables?
Influencing a vendor or supplier outside your organization is which direction of influence?
Influencing a peer in another department who is neither above nor below you is…
What does the project charter do?
options: Formally authorizes the project to begin, letting the PM apply organizational resources once the sponsor signs

03-project-initiation-part-1.q: Which is NOT something the project charter records?
options: Key deliverables, milestones, roles and responsibilities
03-project-initiation-part-1.explain: The charter is high-level. The network diagram comes later from Sequence Activities.

03-project-initiation-part-1.q: In the major project constraints table, which constraint was added beyond the earlier five factors to capture uncertainty?

06-project-planning-part-1.q: How many of the 49 processes are in the Planning process group?
06-project-planning-part-1.explain: Initiating 2, Planning 24, Executing 10, Monitoring & Controlling 12, Closing 1.

06-project-planning-part-1.q: Which knowledge area is the only one that reaches all five process groups?
Which three baselines does the project management plan carry?
The scope baseline is made up of…
options: Project scope statement + WBS + WBS dictionary

06-project-planning-part-1.q: Which process produces the requirements traceability matrix?
"Include course creation and assessment features; explicitly record the excluded capabilities" is an example of which process?
"Gradebook integration has to be done before end-to-end acceptance testing can begin" is an output of thinking from which process?
06-project-planning-part-1.explain: Sequence Activities identifies dependencies; output is the project schedule network diagram.

06-project-planning-part-1.q: Which process rolls up cost estimates and sets the authorized cost baseline?
Which process produces the team charter?
Logging "early pilot recruitment" in the risk register shows that…
options: Risks include opportunities (positive uncertainty) as well as threats
The register is only for vendors
It belongs in the issue log instead

06-project-planning-part-1.q: What distinguishes qualitative from quantitative risk analysis?
options: Qualitative is optional; quantitative is always done
Qualitative ranks individual risks and is always done; quantitative models combined numeric effect and is optional

06-project-planning-part-1.q: Deciding whether to buy a video integration service and setting selection criteria is…
A previous portal cost $80,000 and the new one needs 25% more effort. Analogous estimation gives…
Using PERT, a task has O = 10, M = 15, P = 26 hours. What is E?
In Basic COCOMO, size is measured in ____ and effort in ____.
An aircraft control system with strict timing constraints is a typical ____ COCOMO project.
135 function points at 12 hours per FP gives an effort of…
Why use function point estimation instead of COCOMO early on?
options: It measures functionality delivered to users, so it works before the language/implementation is finalized

06-project-planning-part-1.q: Which estimation method is described as detailed and transparent but time-consuming?

final.q: Writing a book is a project, but printing the same newspaper every day is operations. What makes the difference?
options: The book is temporary and unique; the newspaper is ongoing and repetitive

final.q: A sponsor demands the same scope two months earlier with no extra budget. Which factor is most likely to suffer?
final.explain: With scope, time and cost fixed, quality (or expectations) absorbs the pressure.

final.q: Every one of PMI's 49 processes sits at the intersection of…
options: A process group and a knowledge area

final.q: "Measure progress and evaluate changes against the plan" describes which process group?
Perform Integrated Change Control belongs to which knowledge area and process group?
A PM who owns the project outcome, not just the assigned tasks, is following which principle?
A team judges its work by tickets closed rather than benefit delivered. Which principle are they missing?
A project can't avoid some e-waste, so it reduces it as much as possible. Which sustainability pyramid level is this?
The 49-process / 5-group structure comes from which PMBOK edition?
final.explain: The project management mindset comes from the Eighth Edition.

final.q: Resolving a conflict between two developers with empathy and emotional intelligence is a ____ skill.
Keeping project objectives aligned with the organization's broader strategy is part of…
Which input is used to develop the project charter?
The charter is signed. What can the project manager now do?
options: Apply organizational resources to project activities

final.q: The CFO can cancel your project but rarely asks for updates. On a power/interest grid they are…
In the salience model, "legitimacy" means…
options: The stakeholder is appropriately involved in or impacted by the project
The stakeholder pays for the project

final.q: Persuading senior management to approve extra testing time is which direction of influence?
Influencing is described as…
options: Winning people over to do what's best for the project

final.q: Plan Stakeholder Engagement is the follow-on to which Initiating process?
Most knowledge areas open with a "Plan X Management" process. What does it do?
options: Sets the rules for how X will be defined, estimated and controlled

final.q: Why do planning processes repeat throughout the project?
options: Plans get revisited whenever new information comes in

final.q: "Decompose the assessment module into work packages for quizzes and rubrics" is…
Which process works out which activities are needed for each WBS work package?
Develop Schedule combines which inputs?
options: Activities, dependencies, durations and resource constraints

final.q: "Define accessibility checks, response-time targets and acceptance tests" is…
"Schedule regular sponsor updates and summaries of pilot feedback" is…
"Rank privacy approval delays higher than minor interface polish concerns" is…
"Model the probability of missing the semester launch date" is…
"Assign a mitigation owner to the privacy approval risk" is…
Why is software cost estimation especially hard?
options: Software projects are highly dynamic and don't repeat from one project to the next

final.q: Early in a project there are no detailed requirements, but you have experienced experts and data from similar projects. Which pair of methods fits?
A task could take 4, 6 or 14 days. What is the PERT estimate?
You have reliable KLOC estimates and calibrated coefficients. Which method fits?
In Basic COCOMO, how is duration calculated?
What determines a project's COCOMO category?
options: The development environment and constraints, not just the kind of application

final.q: Which is NOT one of the five function types in function point estimation?
Which method's main limitation is that it's subjective?
Which method's main advantage is that it explicitly addresses uncertainty?
